resources.string: Push-up
Wall push-up
Push away from a wall with your body straight. The easiest way to learn the push-up shape.
Hands at chest height, a little wider than your shoulders\nBody in one line from head to heels\nBring your chest to the wall, then press away
Incline push-up
A push-up with your hands on a bench, table or step. The higher the support, the easier it is.
Hands on the edge, under your shoulders\nSqueeze your glutes to keep your hips level\nLower until your chest touches the edge
Knee push-up
A push-up from your knees, keeping a straight line from knees to head.
Knees on a soft surface, hips forward\nElbows about 45 degrees from your body\nLower your chest, not your hips
Push-up
The classic push-up: hands and toes on the floor, body straight, chest down to a fist\'s height.
Hands under your shoulders, fingers spread\nBrace your stomach so your back stays flat\nElbows back at about 45 degrees, not flared out
Diamond push-up
A push-up with your hands close together under your chest, which shifts the work to your triceps.
Thumbs and index fingers touching under your chest\nKeep elbows close to your sides\nLower until your chest meets your hands
Decline push-up
A push-up with your feet raised on a bench or step, putting more of your weight on your arms.
Feet on the bench, hands on the floor\nKeep your hips in line, not piked up\nLower your forehead towards the floor between your hands
Archer push-up
A wide push-up where one arm does most of the work while the other stays straight to the side.
Hands about twice shoulder width\nBend one arm and keep the other straight\nShift your chest over the working hand
Pseudo-planche push-up
A push-up with your hands turned out beside your waist and your shoulders leaning far forward of them.
Hands beside your waist, fingers turned out\nLean forward before you lower\nKeep the lean all the way down and up
One-arm push-up
A push-up on one hand with feet wide for balance. A long-term goal of the push chain.
Feet wide, free hand behind your back\nWorking hand under your chest, slightly inward\nKeep your shoulders square to the floor
Handstand push-up
Pike push-up
A push-up with your hips high, so your body makes an upside-down V and your shoulders do the pressing.
Walk your feet in until your hips are high\nLower the top of your head between your hands\nPress back up through your shoulders
Elevated pike push-up
A pike push-up with your feet on a bench, closer to a handstand and harder on your shoulders.
Feet on the bench, hips straight above your hands\nLower your head in front of your hands, forming a triangle\nKeep your elbows over your wrists
Wall handstand
Holding a handstand with your chest facing the wall, building strength and comfort upside down.
Walk your feet up the wall as your hands come close\nPush the floor away, arms straight\nRibs in, body in one line
Wall handstand push-up negative
From a wall handstand, lower yourself slowly to your head, then come down and start again.
Take three to five seconds to lower\nHead lands in front of your hands\nUse a cushion under your head at first
Wall handstand push-up
A full push-up in a handstand against the wall, lowering to your head and pressing back up.
Hands shoulder width, a hand\'s length from the wall\nLower under control to a cushion\nPress straight up and lock your arms
Freestanding handstand push-up
A handstand push-up balanced away from any wall.
Find the balance first\nLower to a tripod with your head forward of your hands\nPress up and re-balance at the top
Dip
Bench dip
Dipping with your hands on a bench behind you and your feet on the floor.
Hands at the edge, fingers forward\nKeep your back close to the bench\nLower until your upper arms are level, no further
Support hold
Holding yourself up on straight arms on parallel bars, the top of a dip.
Arms locked straight\nShoulders pushed down, away from your ears\nLegs together, slightly in front
Dip negative
From the support hold, lowering yourself slowly into the bottom of a dip.
Take three to five seconds to lower\nLean slightly forward\nStop when your shoulders are just below your elbows
Dip
Lowering and pressing back up on parallel bars.
Start from a straight-arm support\nLower until your shoulders are just below your elbows\nPress up until your arms are straight
Pull-up
Dead hang
Hanging from a bar with straight arms, building grip and shoulder strength for pulling.
Grip a little wider than your shoulders\nRelax your legs, keep your body still\nBreathe steadily
Scapular pull-up
From a dead hang, pulling your shoulder blades down and back without bending your arms.
Arms stay straight\nLift your chest slightly by pulling your shoulders down\nLower with control
Pull-up negative
Starting with your chin over the bar, lowering yourself slowly to a hang.
Jump or step up to the top\nTake three to five seconds to lower\nFinish in a full hang
Band-assisted pull-up
A pull-up with a resistance band under your knee or foot taking some of your weight.
Loop the band over the bar, then step into it\nPull until your chin is over the bar\nUse a lighter band as you get stronger
Chin-up
A pull-up with your palms facing you, which gets more help from your biceps.
Hands shoulder width, palms towards you\nPull your elbows down to your sides\nChin over the bar, then lower fully
Pull-up
Pulling yourself up from a dead hang until your chin is over the bar, palms facing away.
Hands a little wider than your shoulders\nStart each rep from a full hang\nLead with your chest, not your chin
L-sit pull-up
A pull-up with your legs held straight out in front in an L-sit the whole time.
Legs straight and level before you pull\nPull without letting the legs drop\nLower under control
Typewriter pull-up
Pulling up to the bar, sliding across to one hand and then the other, staying at the top.
Wide grip\nChin stays above the bar as you move\nSlow and level from side to side
Archer pull-up
A wide pull-up towards one hand while the other arm stays nearly straight.
Grip wide\nPull towards one hand, sliding the other arm straight\nAlternate sides each set or each rep
One-arm pull-up negative
From the top of a pull-up, lowering yourself slowly on one arm.
Start at the top with both hands, then let one go\nLower as slowly as you can\nKeep your shoulder pulled down
One-arm pull-up
A full pull-up on one arm. A long-term goal of the pull chain.
Start from a still hang\nTurn your body slightly towards the working arm\nPull your elbow down to your side
Row
Incline row
Pulling your chest to a high bar or sturdy table edge with your body leaning back at an angle.
The more upright you stand, the easier it is\nBody straight from head to heels\nPull your chest to the bar
Horizontal row
Hanging under a waist-high bar with your body straight and heels on the floor, pulling your chest up to it.
Bar at about hip height\nSqueeze your shoulder blades together at the top\nLower until your arms are straight
Feet-elevated row
A horizontal row with your feet on a bench, so your body is level and you lift more of your weight.
Feet on the bench, body level\nKeep your hips up\nPull your chest all the way to the bar
Archer row
A wide row pulling towards one hand while the other arm stays straight.
Grip wide\nPull towards one hand, the other arm stays straight\nKeep your body from twisting
One-arm row
A horizontal row on one arm, with your feet wide to stop your body turning.
Feet wide for balance\nWorking hand in line with your chest\nFight the twist as you pull
Squat
Assisted squat
A squat holding a door frame or sturdy support, using your arms as little as you need.
Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out\nSit back and down as if onto a chair\nPush through your whole foot to stand
Wall sit
Sitting against a wall with your thighs level with the floor, holding the position.
Back flat against the wall\nKnees over your ankles, thighs level\nBreathe steadily while you hold
Bodyweight squat
A full squat with no support, hips going down to at least knee height.
Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out\nKnees travel in the direction of your toes\nChest up, heels down
Split squat
From a long step stance, lowering your back knee towards the floor and standing back up.
Feet a long stride apart\nLower straight down, not forward\nFront knee follows your toes
Bulgarian split squat
A split squat with your back foot raised on a bench, so the front leg works harder.
Back foot laces-down on the bench\nFront foot far enough forward that your knee stays over it\nLower until your back knee nearly touches the floor
Assisted pistol squat
A one-leg squat holding a support, with the other leg out in front.
Hold a door frame or pole\nFree leg straight out in front\nLower slowly on the standing leg
Shrimp squat
A one-leg squat holding your other foot behind you and lowering your back knee to the floor.
Hold your rear foot with the hand on the same side\nLean forward a little for balance\nTouch your knee down softly
Pistol squat
A full one-leg squat with the other leg held straight out in front. A goal of the squat chain.
Arms forward for balance\nHeel stays down the whole way\nGo all the way down, then drive up
Hip hinge
Glute bridge
Lying on your back with knees bent, lifting your hips until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Feet flat, close to your hips\nPush through your heels\nSqueeze your glutes at the top, ribs down
Single-leg glute bridge
A glute bridge on one leg, the other held up straight or bent.
Working foot close to your hip\nKeep your hips level as you lift\nPause for a second at the top
Single-leg hip thrust
A single-leg bridge with your shoulders on a bench, for a bigger range of motion.
Shoulder blades on the bench edge\nChin tucked, eyes forward\nDrive up until your body is level
Sliding leg curl
From a bridge with your heels on a towel or sliders, pulling your heels in and pushing them out again.
Hold the bridge the whole time\nPull your heels towards you\nSlide out slowly
Nordic curl negative
Kneeling with your ankles held down, lowering your body forward as slowly as you can.
Ankles anchored under something sturdy\nBody straight from knees to head\nCatch yourself with your hands, push back up
Nordic curl
Lowering forward from your knees and pulling yourself back up with your hamstrings alone.
Ankles anchored\nHips stay straight, no bending\nLower and rise under full control
Core
Dead bug
Lying on your back with arms and knees up, lowering opposite arm and leg while keeping your back flat.
Press your lower back into the floor\nMove slowly, breathe out as you reach\nAlternate sides
Plank
Holding a straight body on your forearms and toes.
Elbows under your shoulders\nSqueeze your glutes and brace your stomach\nDo not let your hips sag
Tuck hollow hold
Lying on your back with knees pulled in and shoulders lifted, lower back pressed down.
Lower back flat on the floor\nShoulders off the floor, chin slightly in\nArms reaching towards your feet
Hollow body hold
Holding a shallow banana shape on your back: legs straight and low, arms overhead, lower back down.
Lower back stays pressed to the floor\nLegs together and straight\nRaise your legs if your back lifts
Leg raise
Lying knee raise
Lying on your back, bringing your knees to your chest and lowering them slowly.
Hands by your hips\nCurl your hips slightly off the floor at the top\nLower without letting your back arch
Lying leg raise
Lying on your back, raising straight legs to vertical and lowering them slowly.
Legs together and straight\nLower back stays down\nStop just above the floor
Hanging knee raise
Hanging from a bar and raising your knees towards your chest without swinging.
Start from a still hang\nCurl your pelvis up at the top\nLower slowly
Hanging leg raise
Hanging from a bar and raising straight legs to hip height or higher.
Legs straight and together\nNo swinging between reps\nLift until your legs are level
Toes to bar
Hanging from a bar and raising straight legs all the way to touch the bar.
Press the bar down slightly with straight arms\nLift your legs and curl your hips\nLower under control
Handstand
Crow pose
Balancing on your hands with your knees resting on the backs of your upper arms. The first taste of weight on the hands.
Hands flat, fingers spread, shoulder width\nKnees high on your upper arms\nLean forward until your feet float
Wall walk
From a push-up position with your feet at a wall, walking your feet up the wall and your hands in, then back out.
Small steps with hands and feet\nKeep your arms straight and your body tight\nWalk in only as far as you can control
Handstand kick-up
Kicking up towards a handstand on open floor and finding the balance point for a moment, then stepping down.
Hands shoulder width, eyes between them\nKick with one leg, follow with the other\nStep down to the side if you go over
Freestanding handstand
Balancing upside down on your hands without a wall, body in one straight line.
Push the floor away, shoulders by your ears\nSqueeze your legs together, toes pointed\nSteer with your fingertips
Press to handstand
From standing bent over with your hands down, lifting your straight or straddled legs up into a handstand without jumping.
Shoulders lean forward over your hands\nHips rise first, legs follow\nNo jump: press slowly
One-arm handstand
Balancing a handstand on one straight arm, the other free.
Shift your weight fully over one hand first\nStraddle your legs to help balance\nSteer with your fingers
L-sit
Foot-supported L-sit
Sitting with your hands by your hips, pressing down to lift your hips while your heels stay on the floor.
Hands flat beside your hips\nPush down and lift your hips\nShoulders down, away from your ears
Tuck L-sit
Holding yourself up on straight arms with your knees pulled into your chest.
Arms locked straight\nKnees tight to your chest\nPress the floor or handles away
One-leg L-sit
A tuck L-sit with one leg straightened out in front, changing legs each set.
One knee tucked, the other leg straight\nLift the straight leg level with your hips\nChange legs each set
L-sit
Holding yourself up on straight arms with both legs straight out in front, making an L.
Legs straight and together, level with your hips\nPoint your toes\nKeep pushing down through your hands
V-sit
From an L-sit, lifting your straight legs higher until your body makes a V.
Lean your shoulders back a little\nLift your legs as high as you can\nKeep your arms straight
Muscle-up
Chest-to-bar pull-up
A pull-up driven hard enough to bring your chest to the bar: the pull a muscle-up needs.
Start each rep from a full hang\nPull fast and drive your elbows down\nTouch the bar with your chest
Muscle-up negative
From the top of the bar on straight arms, lowering slowly through the dip and the turn to a hang.
Start on top with straight arms\nLower through the dip slowly\nKeep the bar close as you turn under it
Band-assisted muscle-up
A full muscle-up with a band taking some of your weight through the pull and the turn.
Pull high, towards your chest\nLean your chest over the bar quickly\nPress up until your arms are straight
Muscle-up
Pulling yourself up from a hang and over the bar in one movement, finishing on straight arms above it.
Pull explosively, the bar to your chest\nTurn your wrists and lean over the bar\nPress to straight arms
Front lever
Tuck front lever
Hanging from a bar with straight arms, holding your body level with your knees tucked to your chest.
Arms straight, pull the bar down towards your hips\nBack flat and level with the floor\nKnees tight to your chest
Advanced tuck front lever
A tuck front lever with your back flat and your hips opened, knees out at a right angle.
Flatten your back\nPush your knees away until your thighs are level\nKeep pressing the bar down
One-leg front lever
A front lever with one leg straight and the other tucked, changing legs each set.
One leg straight, in line with your body\nThe other knee tucked\nChange legs each set
Straddle front lever
A front lever with both legs straight and spread wide, which shortens the lever.
Legs straight and wide apart\nHips level with your shoulders\nSqueeze your glutes
Front lever
Hanging face up with straight arms and your whole body straight and level with the floor.
Legs together, body in one line\nPull the bar down with straight arms\nHold your hips up
Back lever
Skin the cat
From a hang, lifting your legs through your arms and rolling over backwards until you hang behind the bar, then returning.
Tuck your knees and lift them through your arms\nLower slowly into the stretch behind you\nCome back the same way
German hang
Hanging from the bar at the bottom of a skin the cat, arms behind you, letting your shoulders open.
Ease into the stretch slowly\nKeep your arms straight\nCome out the way you went in
Tuck back lever
Hanging face down behind the bar with straight arms, back level, knees tucked to your chest.
Arms straight, the bar behind your hips\nBack level with the floor\nKnees tight to your chest
Advanced tuck back lever
A tuck back lever with your back flat and your hips opened, knees out at a right angle.
Flatten your back\nPush your knees away until your thighs are level\nArms stay straight
Straddle back lever
A back lever with both legs straight and spread wide.
Legs straight and wide apart\nBody level, face down\nSqueeze your glutes
Back lever
Hanging face down behind the bar with your whole body straight and level with the floor.
Legs together, body in one line\nArms straight, the bar at your hips\nDo not let your hips sag
Planche
Planche lean
From the top of a push-up, leaning your shoulders forward past your hands and holding.
Fingers turned out a little\nLean forward with straight arms\nRound your upper back slightly
Tuck planche
Balancing on straight arms with your feet off the floor and your knees tucked under your body.
Arms locked straight\nLean forward until your feet lift\nKnees tucked, hips high
Advanced tuck planche
A tuck planche with your back flat and your hips level with your shoulders.
Flatten your back\nHips level with your shoulders\nPush the floor away
Straddle planche
Balancing on straight arms with your body level and your legs straight and spread wide.
Legs straight and wide apart\nBody level with the floor\nLean until you balance over your hands
Planche
Balancing on straight arms with your whole body straight and level above the floor.
Legs together, body in one line\nArms straight, shoulders forward of your hands\nSqueeze everything
Side core
Knee side plank
Lying on your side, propped on one forearm with your knees bent, lifting your hips into a straight line.
Elbow under your shoulder\nHips up, in line with your knees and shoulders\nSwitch sides each set
Side plank
Holding your body straight and sideways on one forearm and the edge of your feet.
Elbow under your shoulder\nFeet stacked, body in one line\nDo not let your hips drop
Side plank hip lift
From a side plank, lowering your hips towards the floor and lifting them back up past straight.
Elbow under your shoulder\nLower under control\nLift from your side, not your shoulder
Star side plank
A side plank on a straight arm with your top leg and top arm raised.
Supporting arm straight, hand under your shoulder\nLift your top leg as high as you can\nKeep your hips up
Human flag
Vertical flag
Gripping a pole with one hand high and one low, lifting your feet and holding your body upright beside it.
Hands wider than your shoulders\nPull with the top arm, push with the bottom arm\nSwitch hands each set
Tuck flag
Holding your body sideways off a pole with your knees tucked to your chest.
Bottom arm locked straight\nPush hard with the bottom arm\nKnees tight to your chest
One-leg flag
A tuck flag with the top leg straight out to the side and the other knee still tucked.
Top leg straight, in line with your body\nBottom arm locked\nHips stay up
Straddle flag
Holding your body level beside a pole with both legs straight and spread wide.
Legs straight and wide apart\nBody level with the floor\nPush and pull at the same time
Human flag
Holding your whole body straight and level out to the side of a pole.
Legs together, body in one line\nBottom arm locked straight\nSqueeze everything
Back bridge
Tabletop bridge
Sitting with your hands behind you and knees bent, lifting your hips until your body is flat like a table.
Hands under your shoulders, fingers towards your feet\nKnees over your ankles\nHips up level with your shoulders
Angled bridge
Lying back with your hands on a bench behind your head, pushing up into an arch with the bench taking some weight.
Hands by your head, fingers towards your feet\nPush through your hands and feet together\nArch from your upper back, not only your lower back
Full bridge
Lying on your back with your hands by your head, pushing up into a full arch on straight arms.
Hands by your head, fingers towards your feet\nStraighten your arms fully\nPush your chest towards the wall behind you
Bridge push-up
From the floor, pushing up into a full bridge and lowering back down under control.
Start with your head off the floor\nPress up until your arms are straight\nLower slowly, do not drop onto your head
One-leg bridge
A full bridge with one leg lifted straight up, switching legs each set.
Shift your weight onto the standing leg first\nLift the other leg straight\nKeep your hips level and high
Burpee
Step-back burpee
From standing, squatting to put your hands down, stepping back to a plank one foot at a time, then stepping in and standing.
Hands flat beside your feet\nStep back and in one foot at a time\nStand up tall at the end
Squat thrust
From a squat with your hands down, jumping both feet back to a plank and jumping them in again.
Hands flat beside your feet\nLand in a straight plank, hips level\nJump your feet in close to your hands
Burpee
A squat thrust that finishes with a jump straight up, hands over your head.
Jump your feet back to a plank\nJump them in, then jump up\nLand softly on bent knees
Push-up burpee
A burpee with a full push-up when you land in the plank.
Land in a straight plank\nChest to the floor, body in one line\nJump in and up without a pause
Tuck-jump burpee
A push-up burpee that finishes with a tuck jump, knees pulled to your chest.
Drive your knees up to your chest\nLand softly on bent knees\nKeep the push-up full
Calf raise
Calf raise
Standing tall and rising onto the balls of your feet, then lowering your heels again.
Rise as high as you can\nPause for a moment at the top\nLower slowly
Elevated calf raise
A calf raise with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step, so your heels can drop below it.
Let your heels sink for a full stretch\nRise all the way up\nHold something for balance if you need to
Single-leg calf raise
A calf raise on one foot, a hand on the wall for balance.
Working knee straight but not locked\nRise as high as you can\nLower slowly
Elevated single-leg calf raise
A single-leg calf raise from the edge of a step, through the full range.
Heel sinks below the step\nRise to the very top\nSlow on the way down
Pogo hop
Small, quick hops on the balls of your feet, with your knees nearly straight.
Stay on the balls of your feet\nKeep the hops low and springy\nLand quietly
Lunge
Reverse lunge
Stepping one foot back and lowering until the back knee nearly touches the floor, then standing up again.
Step back far enough for both knees to bend to a right angle\nFront knee over the foot\nPush through the front heel
Walking lunge
Lunging forward with each step, alternating legs as you walk.
Long steps\nBack knee nearly touches the floor\nStay tall through your chest
Lateral lunge
Stepping wide to one side and sitting back into that hip, the other leg straight.
Toes point forward\nSit back into the bent hip\nKeep the straight leg\'s foot flat
Cossack squat
From a wide stance, squatting all the way down over one leg while the other stays straight, toes up.
Heel of the bent leg stays down\nStraight leg\'s toes point up\nMove slowly from side to side
Sissy squat
Holding a wall for balance and leaning back as your knees travel forward, lowering on your toes.
Body straight from knees to shoulders\nRise onto your toes as you lower\nGo only as deep as you control
Explosive
Jump squat
Squatting down and jumping straight up as high as you can, landing softly into the next squat.
Swing your arms to help\nJump as high as you can\nLand softly on bent knees
Box jump
Jumping from the floor onto a sturdy box or bench, landing in a quiet squat, then stepping down.
Use something that will not tip or slide\nLand with your whole foot on top\nStep down, do not jump down
Clap push-up
A push-up driven hard enough for your hands to leave the floor and clap before you land.
Push the floor away fast\nClap quickly, hands back under your shoulders\nLand with soft elbows
Explosive pull-up
Pulling up as fast as you can, aiming to bring your chest to the bar.
Start from a dead hang\nPull hard and fast\nLower under control
Superman push-up
A push-up so explosive that your hands and feet leave the floor together.
Brace your whole body\nDrive from hands and toes at once\nLand on hands and feet together
Rollout and dragon flag
Kneeling rollout
Kneeling with your hands on a towel, sliders or an ab wheel, rolling forward until your body is nearly straight and back.
Ribs down, back flat\nRoll only as far as you can keep it flat\nPull back with your stomach, not your hips
Tuck dragon flag
Lying on a bench and holding behind your head, lifting your body up onto your shoulders with your knees tucked.
Grip the bench firmly behind your head\nWeight on your upper back, not your neck\nKnees tucked, hips off the bench
Dragon flag negative
From the top of a dragon flag, lowering your straight body to the bench as slowly as you can.
Body straight from shoulders to feet\nLower slowly, no bend at the hips\nReset at the top each time
Standing rollout
A rollout from standing, rolling out until your body is straight above the floor and back up.
Ribs down the whole way\nArms long\nRoll back with your stomach
Dragon flag
Lowering and raising your straight body from your shoulders on a bench, without touching down.
Body straight from shoulders to feet\nWeight on your upper back\nLower and raise under control
Rotation
Russian twist
Sitting leaning back with your feet down or lifted, turning your shoulders from side to side.
Lean back with a straight back\nTurn your shoulders, not only your arms\nEach side counts as one
Lying windshield wiper
Lying on your back with your legs straight up, lowering them to one side and then the other.
Arms out wide, shoulders down\nLegs together\nGo only as low as you control
Hanging knee wiper
Hanging with your knees raised to your chest, swinging them from side to side.
Knees high the whole time\nTurn from your waist\nNo swinging of the body
Hanging windshield wiper
Hanging with your feet raised to the bar, sweeping your straight legs from side to side.
Feet up near the bar\nLegs straight and together\nSlow and controlled
Back extension
Bird dog
On hands and knees, reaching one arm forward and the opposite leg back, then switching.
Back flat, hips level\nReach long, not high\nPause, then switch sides
Superman hold
Lying face down and lifting your arms, chest and legs off the floor together.
Look at the floor, neck long\nSqueeze your glutes\nLift as one piece
Reverse snow angel
Lying face down with your chest lifted, sweeping your arms from your sides to overhead and back.
Chest slightly lifted the whole time\nThumbs up, arms off the floor\nSlow sweeps
Bench back extension
Lying face down with your hips at the end of a bench and your ankles held, lowering your upper body and lifting it level.
Hips at the edge of the bench\nLift until your body is straight, no higher\nLower slowly
Reverse hyperextension
Lying face down on a bench with your hips at the edge, lifting your straight legs up level with your body.
Hold the bench firmly\nLegs straight and together\nLift to level and lower slowly
Grip
Towel hang
Hanging from two towels draped over the bar, gripping the cloth.
Towels thrown over the bar, one per hand\nSqueeze hard\nShoulders engaged, not shrugged
Assisted one-arm hang
Hanging from one hand with only a few fingers of the other hand helping.
Most of your weight on one hand\nUse as few helping fingers as you can\nSwitch hands each set
One-arm dead hang
Hanging from one hand with your shoulder engaged.
Shoulder pulled down, not hanging loose\nFree hand by your side\nSwitch hands each set
Towel pull-up
A pull-up holding two towels draped over the bar.
Grip the towels hard\nPull your chest up between your hands\nLower under control
Rings
Ring push-up
A push-up with your hands on gymnastic rings hung a little above the floor.
Rings steady under your shoulders\nBody straight\nTurn the rings out a little at the top
Ring support hold
Holding yourself above the rings on straight arms, the rings close to your body.
Arms locked straight\nRings pressed against your sides\nTurn the rings out as you get steadier
False-grip hang
Hanging from the rings with your wrists over them, the grip a muscle-up needs.
Ring sits in the heel of your hand\nWrists bent over the rings\nShoulders engaged
Ring dip
A dip on rings, keeping them steady and close as you lower and press back up.
Start from a steady support\nRings close to your body\nPress to straight arms and turn the rings out
Ring muscle-up
From a false-grip hang, pulling and turning over the rings into a support, in one movement.
False grip from the start\nPull the rings to your lower chest\nLean forward over the rings and press out
Lower body mobility
Deep squat hold
Sitting all the way down in a squat with your heels flat, and staying there.
Heels stay down\nKnees follow your toes\nChest up, breathe slowly
Couch stretch
Kneeling with your back shin up a wall and the front foot forward, opening the front of the hip.
Back knee close to the wall\nSqueeze the glute of the back leg\nStay tall, do not arch
Standing pike fold
Standing with straight legs and folding forward from the hips.
Knees straight but soft\nFold from the hips, not the back\nLet your head hang
Seated pike compression
Sitting with straight legs, hands beside your knees, lifting your feet off the floor by pulling your legs to your chest.
Legs straight and together\nLean forward over your legs\nLift with your stomach, not by leaning back
Pancake
Sitting with your legs straight and wide, folding forward between them.
Knees and toes point up\nTilt from the hips\nWalk your hands forward slowly
Front split
Sliding one leg forward and the other back until your hips sink towards the floor.
Hips square to the front\nSupport yourself with your hands or blocks\nEase down, never bounce
Middle split
Sliding both legs out to the sides until your hips sink towards the floor.
Knees and toes point up or forward\nSupport yourself with your hands\nEase down, never bounce
Shoulder and wrist mobility
Wrist rocks
On hands and knees, rocking your weight gently forward and back over your hands, palms flat.
Palms flat, fingers spread\nRock slowly within comfort\nAlso try fingers turned out and back
Shoulder dislocate
Holding a band or towel wide in front, lifting it over your head and behind you with straight arms, and back.
Arms straight the whole way\nGrip wide enough to pass easily\nNarrow the grip slowly over weeks
Wall slide
Back and arms against a wall, sliding your arms up overhead and down, keeping them touching the wall.
Lower back against the wall\nElbows and wrists touch the wall\nSlide slowly
Puppy pose
On hands and knees, walking your hands forward and sinking your chest towards the floor, hips over knees.
Hips stay above your knees\nArms long\nLet your chest sink as you breathe out
